candidates.exact_span:
The facility is a POTW treating sanitary wastewater. POTW’s have technology based ELG’s
established at 40 CFR Part 133, Secondary Treatment Regulation. Pollutants with ELG’s
established in this Chapter are BOD5, TSS and pH.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that Part 133 secondary-treatment ELGs govern this facility and limits the set of pollutants with technology-based numeric limits subject to compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
BOD5 limits of 30 mg/L for the 30-day
average and 45 mg/L for the 7-day average and 85% percent (minimum) removal are found at 40
CFR §133.102(a).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies BOD5 concentration and percent-removal numeric limits and the averaging periods used to select the applicable limit for a reported measurement.

candidates.exact_span:
TSS limits, 30 mg/L for the 30-day average and 45 mg/L for the 7-day
average, and 85% percent (minimum) removal, are, also, found at 40 CFR §133.102(b).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies TSS concentration and percent-removal numeric limits and the averaging periods used to select the applicable limit for a reported measurement.

candidates.exact_span:
ELG’s
for pH are between 6-9 s.u. and are found at 40 CFR §133.102(c).
candidates.computation_change_reason: States the technology-based pH numeric range; interpretation of whether this or a more restrictive WQS value governs changes the applicable pH limit for comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
Regulations at 40 CFR
§122.45(f)(1) require all pollutants limited in permits to have limits expressed in terms of mass
such as pounds per day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether enforceable limits must be evaluated as mass-based (lbs/day) rather than concentration-only for pollutants limited in the permit.

candidates.exact_span:
When determining mass limits for POTW’s, the plant’s design flow is
used to establish the mass load.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selects design flow (rather than measured or other flow basis) as the input for converting concentration limits to applicable mass limits.

candidates.exact_span: Loading in lbs/day = pollutant concentration in mg/L * 8.345 lbs/gal * design flow in MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the conversion formula used to compute applicable mass-based discharge limits from concentration limits and design flow.

candidates.exact_span: Final Effluent Limits 6.67 MGD design flow
candidates.computation_change_reason: Fixes the design flow value (6.67 MGD) used in the stated mass-limit calculations and summary table.
States the facility-specific final BOD5 mass and concentration limits for 30-day and 7-day averaging periods used in exceedance evaluation.
States the facility-specific final TSS mass and concentration limits for 30-day and 7-day averaging periods used in exceedance evaluation.
Imposes a minimum BOD5 percent-removal numeric limit that must be evaluated separately from concentration/mass limits.
Imposes a minimum TSS percent-removal numeric limit that must be evaluated separately from concentration/mass limits.

candidates.exact_span:
(1) % removal is calculated using the following equation: [(average monthly influent concentration – average
    monthly effluent concentration) ÷ average monthly influent concentration] * 100.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines how percent-removal compliance is computed from influent and effluent data; different readings affect whether removal limits are met and how missing influent/effluent results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Flow                       N/A                N/A               Measure MGD         Measure MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates flow must be measured (not merely limited numerically) for 30-day and 7-day averaging periods, affecting whether flow monitoring was required.
States the summary-table pH numeric limit (6.6–9.0 s.u.), which differs from the 6–9 s.u. ELG text and affects which pH range is used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
(2) Stream segment specific (20.6.4.401 NMAC) WQS, which are more restrictive than pH technology-based
    limits, 6-9 s.u.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies a water-quality-standard basis for pH that is more restrictive than technology-based limits; interpretation determines whether WQS (6.6–9.0) or ELG (6–9) limits apply.
